[EFFECT] The day of the week has a non-monotonic, highly variable effect on predicted demand. Weekends — especially Sunday and Saturday — show the widest range of contributions, with some hours on those days strongly boosting demand (up to ~+0.6 in log units) while other hours on the same days suppress it significantly (down to ~−0.9 on Sundays). Midweek days (Monday–Friday) have a narrower range of contributions, centered closer to neutral. There is no simple "weekdays are higher/lower than weekends" pattern; it strongly depends on the time of day.

[IMPORTANCE] Weekday is the 4th most important feature out of 9, making it a moderately strong driver of predicted hourly demand — meaningful but below the top predictors like hour of day or temperature.

[RECOMMENDATION] Because weekends — particularly Sundays — show both the highest peaks and deepest troughs in demand across hours, staffing and bike redistribution plans should be tailored hour-by-hour for weekend days rather than treating the whole weekend uniformly.
